items.title: Aquarium Boka – Exploring Adriatic Marine Biodiversity
items.excerpt: A promotional video presenting Aquarium Boka and the EXChAngE project’s contribution to marine biodiversity awareness and sustainable cross-border tourism.
items.body:
Discover Aquarium Boka in Kotor through a promotional video presenting it as one of the visitor attractions enhanced through the EU co-funded EXChAngE project—Explore Cross-border Aquatic Biodiversity.

At the Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro, project investments supported interior renovation, two new aquarium tanks, improved water conditioning and an open-air exhibition. These improvements strengthened Aquarium Boka’s capacity to introduce visitors to Adriatic marine biodiversity and the importance of its conservation.

Through the Blue Pass tourism product, EXChAngE connected Aquarium Boka with aquatic biodiversity and cultural heritage attractions in Dubrovnik, Hutovo Blato and Mostar, supporting a shared cross-border tourism offer.

As Project Manager for the Institute of Marine Biology from February 2021 to August 2022, I supported project implementation, procurement documentation and reporting.

items.title: EXChAngE Blue Pass – Discover Cross-Border Aquatic Heritage
items.excerpt: Discover the Blue Pass, a joint tourism product connecting aquatic biodiversity and cultural heritage attractions across Croatia, Montenegro, and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
items.body:
This video presents the main output of the EXChAngE project—Explore Cross-border Aquatic Biodiversity: the Blue Pass, a joint tourism product connecting four thematic routes across three countries.

The routes bring together Dubrovnik and its Aquarium in Croatia, Kotor and Aquarium Boka in Montenegro, and the Hutovo Blato Aqua Path and Mostar Aqua Path in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Available at project partners’ sales points, the Blue Pass encourages visitors to explore the region’s connected natural and cultural heritage.

Led by the University of Dubrovnik’s Institute for Marine and Coastal Research, the five-partner project strengthened and diversified the cross-border tourism offer while supporting better management and sustainable use of shared heritage. EXChAngE received EU co-financing through the Interreg IPA Cross-border Cooperation Programme Croatia–Bosnia and Herzegovina–Montenegro 2014–2020.

As Project Manager for the Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro, from February 2021 to August 2022, I supported project implementation, procurement documentation and reporting.

items.title: Blue Growth Cluster – Connecting Montenegro’s Blue Economy
items.excerpt: An introduction to Montenegro’s Blue Growth Cluster, connecting businesses and supporting technology transfer, skills development and cooperation across blue economy sectors.
items.body:
This June 2023 video introduces the Montenegrin Blue Growth Cluster, established in Kotor to strengthen the competitiveness of businesses in fisheries, aquaculture, tourism and maritime transport.

The cluster promotes technology transfer, innovative education and skills development, helping members respond to market needs and contribute to a sustainable blue economy.

Cooperation with other Adriatic clusters offers opportunities to exchange knowledge, develop partnerships and connect Montenegro’s blue economy with regional and international markets.

items.title: AdriBioPro2026 – Conference Highlights
items.excerpt: A visual journey through AdriBioPro2026, capturing four days of science, dialogue and cooperation for Adriatic biodiversity protection and sustainable blue growth.
items.body:
This promotional video captures highlights from the Fourth International Conference on Adriatic Biodiversity Protection—AdriBioPro2026, held from 22 to 25 September 2026 in Kotor, Montenegro.

Featuring footage from across the conference programme, the video brings together moments from scientific sessions, plenary lectures, poster presentations, networking, side events and study visits at the Institute of Marine Biology and Hyatt Regency Kotor Bay.

The conference connected scientists, policymakers, stakeholders and industry representatives to explore marine biodiversity conservation, fisheries and aquaculture, pollution and climate resilience, marine monitoring technologies, and public awareness.

Presented without on-screen text, the video offers a visual record of the people, places and exchanges that shaped four days of regional cooperation for a resilient Adriatic Sea.
